questions.text: Why are Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, and Sulu assigned to Zone 1 (Z = 0.2) while the rest of the Philippines — including Batanes — is Zone 2 (Z = 0.4)?

options.text: These provinces have lower population density and therefore lower design demand, which affects the zoning classification.
These provinces are geologically distant from the main Philippine Fault system and active subduction zones that characterize the Ring of Fire corridor.
These provinces experience frequent minor earthquakes, so a lower Z factor is justified due to the reduced risk of major seismic events.
Zone assignment is based on coastal proximity, not seismic hazard, which is a common misconception.

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The Zone 1 provinces (Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, Sulu) are geologically separated from the central Philippine Fault and major subduction interfaces. They have lower historical earthquake frequency and magnitude potential. Population density is irrelevant to zone assignment; seismic hazard is the determinant. Batanes is in Zone 4 (Z = 0.4) per NSCP 2010 TABLE 208-3, likely due to its proximity to active fault systems and subduction zones in the northern Philippine region.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A building is designed in Manila. Which seismic zone and Z factor apply?

options.text: Zone 1, Z = 0.2
Zone 2, Z = 0.2
Zone 2, Z = 0.4
Zone 3, Z = 0.6

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Manila (and the entire Luzon spine including Batanes) is in Zone 2 with Z = 0.4. The Philippines uses a 2-zone system; there is no Zone 3.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: According to the NSCP 2015, how many seismic zones does the Philippines use, and what are the corresponding Z factors?

options.text: Three zones: Z = 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, which is not aligned with the current zoning system
Two zones: Z = 0.2 (Zone 1) and Z = 0.4 (Zone 2)
Four zones: Z = 0.15, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, which is an incorrect representation of the zoning system
One zone: Z = 0.3 (uniform nationwide), which oversimplifies the seismic zoning approach

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The NSCP 2015 employs a 2-zone system: Zone 1 (Z = 0.2) for Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, and Sulu, and Zone 2 (Z = 0.4) for all other locations including Batanes.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: Which statement correctly characterizes the seismic hazard difference between Zone 1 and Zone 2?

options.text: Zone 1 and Zone 2 have equal hazard; the Z factors are arbitrary and do not reflect actual seismic activity.
Zone 2 is twice as hazardous as Zone 1, reflecting higher earthquake frequency and magnitude potential.
Zone 1 is more hazardous because it has fewer buildings and therefore lower seismic demand, which paradoxically increases risk.
The zones alternate geographically; there is no pattern to their distribution, making hazard assessment unreliable.

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Zone 2 (Z = 0.4) is assigned twice the seismic hazard coefficient as Zone 1 (Z = 0.2) because it encompasses the Philippine Fault system, subduction zones, and major active faults. Zone 1 provinces (Palawan, Tawi-Tawi, Sulu) are geologically separated from the main Ring of Fire corridor.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: A design team must choose between two otherwise identical building designs—one optimized for Zone 1 seismic forces and one for Zone 2. The Zone 1 design uses lighter framing and reduces lateral bracing. If the building is later constructed in a Zone 2 location, what is the structural consequence?

options.text: The building will be adequately designed because seismic forces scale proportionally with member size, which is a misunderstanding of seismic design principles
The building will be under-designed for lateral forces. The lateral stiffness and strength are insufficient to withstand Zone 2 demands, which are twice those of Zone 1.
The difference in Z factors is negligible and can be overlooked in the field, which is incorrect as it disregards safety standards
The building code does not enforce zone compliance, so construction may proceed without modification, which is a misinterpretation of code requirements

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The design base shear V = Z × I × C × W scales directly with Z. A Zone 1 design assumes V(Zone1) = 0.2 × I × C × W. Constructing it in Zone 2 means the actual demand is V(Zone2) = 0.4 × I × C × W—double the designed capacity. Under-design and potential failure result.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: The NSCP 2015 introduced spectral acceleration maps (Ss, S1) based on updated seismic hazard analysis. How does this relate to the 2-zone system with Z = 0.2 and Z = 0.4?

options.text: The spectral acceleration maps replace the zone system entirely; Z factors are obsolete and should not be used.

Verify with NSCP 2015 official documentation whether the 2-zone Z-factor system and spectral acceleration maps coexist or if one supersedes the other. Do not assert LEA curriculum scope without official confirmation.
Spectral accelerations are calculated from Z factors using a fixed formula, which is universally applicable across all regions.
The two approaches are identical; Z = 0.2 always corresponds to the same Ss value regardless of location, which simplifies the design process.

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The NSCP 2015 retained the 2-zone system for backward compatibility and simplicity, while also providing spectral acceleration maps for more detailed site-specific hazard analysis. The LEA tests the 2-zone Z factor approach because it is the historically established and widely taught system. Designers should verify which approach applies to their jurisdiction or regulatory context.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: An engineer is tasked with designing a resort facility in Davao City. Based on the NSCP 2-zone seismic system, what is the seismic zone coefficient Z to be used?

options.text: Z = 0.2 (Zone 1)
Z = 0.3 (intermediate hazard)
Z = 0.4 (Zone 2)
Z = 0.5 (very high hazard)

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.b: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: Davao City is in Mindanao. Most of Mindanao (including Davao del Norte and Davao del Sur) is assigned to Zone 4 with Z = 0.4. Only Sulu, Tawi-Tawi, and Palawan are in Zone 2 with Z = 0.2. The NSCP uses only two zone coefficients: 0.2 and 0.4. There are no intermediate values.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.

questions.text: How many times greater is the design base shear for a building in Zone 2 compared to an identical building in Zone 1, if all other parameters (I, C, W) are held constant?

options.text: 1.2 times
2.0 times
2.5 times
4.0 times

rationale.a: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.c: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.d: This option is incorrect. Review the correct answer above.
rationale.correct: The design base shear is V = Z × I × C × W. Zone 2 has Z = 0.4; Zone 1 has Z = 0.2. The ratio is 0.4 / 0.2 = 2.0.
rationale.takeaway: Review the correct answer and associated code provision.
